_meta.name: feature-graph
_meta.status: DRAFT — v0.5 vocabulary grown from the REAL production parts in drawing-samples/ (IR-ADR-007): the 1-1 bracket's recorded VOCABULARY_GAP list (path sketch profile, offset datum plane, up_to_surface end condition, edge fillet + edge reference model, construction geometry); v0.5.1 adds the 1-2 flange's gap list (revolve with in-sketch axis, circular_pattern with datum-intersection axis + runtime seed-feature reference). Do NOT freeze before the MAT v1 validation set arrives; v0.6.0 adds the ASSEMBLY sub-vocabulary (component + mate — Phase B, ADR-047), grown from the real assembly samples in drawing-samples/assembly/. v0.7.0 (the FORWARD Feature Graph session, IR-ADR-017) deliberately overrides the grow-from-real-parts mantra ONCE to cover the FULL existing part tool surface: sweep, linear_pattern, ellipse/spline profile primitives, graph-level material, edge_flange simple length mode. Known tool-surface limits recorded there (revolve/sweep/loft are boss-only; linear pattern D2 unwired). v0.7.1 (audit-A1) adds NO vocabulary — it PROMOTES eight closed vocabulary sets that existed only as prose (assembly_node_types, mate_types, mate_alignments, anchor_kinds_face/edge, pattern_directions, chamfer_types, bend_positions, edge_flange_positions) plus the two grammar sets (body_producers, feature_producers) into covered_subset as real arrays, so the schema<->ir_schema.py contract test can machine-diff them. Motivation: circular_pattern's seed list had silently rotted to five stale types since 0.7.0 — prose cannot be tested. v0.7.2 (2026-07-30, IR-ADR-019 follow-up) likewise adds NO vocabulary — it DOCUMENTS `extrude.reversed`, which lowering.py has mapped to the tool's `reverse` param and ir_schema.py has validated as a boolean since v0.5, but which the registry never listed. It was found by reading the COMPILER SOURCE instead of the registry — exactly the inversion audit-A1 exists to prevent, and a blind spot audit-A1 cannot catch because it diffs covered_subset ARRAYS while per-param fields are prose by design. No compiler or validator change; graphs that already used the flag are unaffected. v0.8.0 (2026-10-28, IR-ADR-021, the SHEET-METAL DFM session) adds the vocabulary of the typed sheet-metal tools built since: hem, break_corner, closed_corner, corner_relief, miter_flange, gusset, jog, tab_slot, move_face, forming_tool, lofted_bend, swept_flange, from_flat, unfold, fold, flat_pattern, sheet_metal_settings, delete_face, offset_surface, surface_extrude, surface_cut, convert_to_sheet_metal; gauge tables on the base flange, extrude.merge and a radius per fillet edge. The new nodes are STRICT (an unknown field is an error) and their tools' own `verified` verdict is enforced. Table driven: pycompiler/sheetmetal_nodes.py; the contract test diffs every closed set AND every node's field names.
_meta.role: CAD-NEUTRAL intermediate representation (IR). The host AI (Planner) emits this; the deterministic compiler/solidworks lowers it to tool calls. The model NEVER emits raw tool sequences.
_meta.doubles_as: Capability registry — the set of supported feature node types + params IS the capability list. The Planner validates intent against this single artifact (no separate chatty discovery protocol).

graph.schema_version: string (required — IR schema version this graph targets)
graph.units: string (fixed: 'meters' — all lengths are SI meters, matching execution layer)
graph.nodes: array of feature nodes (ordered; order defines build sequence — tree order is law, recipe.md C1)
graph.fully_define_sketches: boolean (optional, default false) — USER RULE (Phase 7 post-mortem): EVERY sketch fully defined, even a hole sketch. true makes the compiler add ONE strict sketch_fully_define after the entities of every `sketch` node and before the cut of every `hole` node (dimensions to the origin, diameters / radii; the sketch ends at constrained_status 3 or the node stops with UNVERIFIED). A node's own `fully_define` wins. Default off so that a replay of an analysed part keeps the original's sketches as they are - a FORWARD graph sets it to true.
graph.material: object (optional, PART graphs only — {name: 'exact library material name, e.g. 1060 Alloy', library?: 'material database, default SolidWorks Materials'}. Material is DOCUMENT state, not a tree feature, so it lives at graph level, never as a node; the compiler applies it via ONE set_part_material call AFTER the last node. Rejected on assembly graphs.)
graph._params: object (optional, additive, IGNORED by the compiler — the lifted parameter map {param_name: {node, field, value_si}} per recipe.md C3)

node_common.id: string (required — stable node id, e.g. 'n1'; used as a reference target by later nodes)
node_common.type: string (required — feature type discriminator; must be one of the registered types below)
node_common.ref: reference object (optional — where this feature attaches; see reference_model). Omitted = canonical default datum.

reference_model._note: Still the make-or-break part of the IR (persistent/topological naming, P1.3). v0.5 adds GEOMETRIC ANCHORS (decided with the user 2026-07-04, HYBRID form): a 3D point recorded from the ORIGINAL part's analyze_model read, resolved DETERMINISTICALLY against the rebuilt geometry at compile time, plus an optional semantic 'hint' that the compiler NEVER reads — it collects design data for the future semantic reference model (P1.3). Anchors are exact for fresh-doc replay but NOT durable across edits — that honest limitation is the P1.3 forcing function.
reference_model.offset: number (optional, on a datum ref — SIGNED offset in meters along the datum normal; != 0 means the sketch sits on a parallel reference plane the compiler creates via add_reference_geometry, e.g. the recipe's plane {ref:'Front Plane', offset:0.003})

node_face.node: string — id of an earlier node
node_face.selector: string — semantic face selector resolved at compile time by the reference resolver: 'top' (v0.5: only 'top')

reference_model.position: string — semantic position on the referenced entity: 'center' (v0.5: only 'center')

face_anchor.near: [x, y, z] — a 3D point (meters) ON the target face's plane, from the ORIGINAL part's analyze_model(faces) representative point. Resolved by plane-containment match (|(near-point)·normal| <= tol) with nearest-representative-point tiebreak among coplanar faces.
face_anchor.hint: string (optional — semantic description for P1.3 data collection, e.g. 'top of the 3mm base plate'; NOT read by the compiler)

edge_anchor.near: [x, y, z] — a 3D point (meters) at the target edge's MIDPOINT, from the ORIGINAL part's analyze_model(edges) mid. Resolved by nearest-mid within a tolerance ball; >1 edge in the ball = REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS, 0 = REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED.
edge_anchor.hint: string (optional — semantic description for P1.3 data collection, e.g. 'slot inner corner'; NOT read by the compiler)

covered_subset.datum_offset: any signed number of meters (0/omitted = the datum plane itself)
covered_subset._note: The subset pycompiler compiles today (key renamed from v05_covered_subset at 0.7.0 — the version lives in _meta, not the key). Outside it the compiler rejects the graph at structural-validation time (no silent gaps). Superset of the v0-exp subset (box+hole fixture still compiles unchanged). CONTRACT (0.7.1, audit-A1): every ARRAY in this block is machine-diffed against the matching frozenset in compiler/solidworks/pycompiler/ir_schema.py by pycompiler/tests/test_ir_schema_contract.py — both directions, exact set equality. Adding a token on one side alone FAILS CI. The prose keys (_note, datum_offset, assumptions) are deliberately NOT contract; per-param types/ranges live in ir_schema.py code and are exercised by the pycompiler suite, not by string-parsing this file.
covered_subset._grammar_note: body_producers = node types whose body a 'hole' may reference (ref.node_face.node). feature_producers = node types that CREATE a named feature, so they are valid seeds for linear_pattern/circular_pattern/mirror (the compiler substitutes the seed's runtime feature name). Patterns are producers themselves — that is what lets a grid compose as a pattern OF a pattern.
covered_subset.assumptions: box centred on the datum origin ('center' -> sketch (0,0)); 'top' bound to global +Y; single body. Path-profile sketches carry EXACT 2D coordinates (from analyze_model(sketch)) — the sketch plane's 2D frame is assumed identical between original and rebuild (same datum/offset => same frame). General 3D-point->sketch-2D resolution for arbitrary faces remains P1.5 option B.

feature_types._note: Profile and operation are SEPARATED on purpose (avoids combinatorial type explosion like 'extruded_circle' + 'extruded_rectangle' + 'revolved_circle'...). Key renamed from feature_types_v05 at 0.7.0 — the version lives in _meta.

box.description: Rectangular boss convenience node — a single IR node that the compiler lowers to many tool calls (create_sketch on the datum + a centred rectangle + a boss extrude). The clearest demonstration of one feature -> many ops.
box.ref: datum (the base plane the box is built on; default 'top')
box.width: number — meters (along the datum's local X)
box.depth: number — meters (along the datum's local Y)

sketch.description: A 2D profile on a plane. Entities are profile primitives, not tools. v0.5 adds PATH profiles: free line/arc chains with exact coordinates (the recipe's 7-line+2-arc bracket outline), plus construction scaffolding. Primitives sharing identical endpoint coordinates close the contour — do NOT add constraints (frozen-coordinate rebuild, see add_sketch_entity guidance).
sketch.from_edges: array of anchors { near: [x,y,z], hint? } (optional; then `profile` is optional) — a MASTER-DRIVEN sketch (user rule: master sketches and the primary driving dimensions come from the SURFACE construction, they are not retyped): the master body's edges at these points (the LOD <= 100 base shape, a solid or a surface, in the geometry state when this node runs) are CONVERTED into the sketch (Convert Entities, one strict sketch_convert_entities right after the sketch is created), so the master's dimensions drive the profile. A `profile` may still add entities after the conversion.
sketch.fully_define: boolean (optional) — overrides the graph's fully_define_sketches for this sketch: true = ONE strict sketch_fully_define after the entities (the sketch ends fully defined), false = leave it as drawn
sketch.ref: datum + optional offset (the sketch plane; offset != 0 => the compiler prefers an existing face on that plane, else creates a parallel reference plane) OR — since v0.5.5, for sketches on NON-axis-aligned support (a bent flange's face, 4-1's Sketch13/16) — { face: face_anchor }: the compiler resolves the anchor via analyze_model(faces) plane-containment (resolve_face_by_anchor) and sketches ON that face (create_sketch on_face). Record the ORIGINAL sketch's `frame` — the frame transform (IR-ADR-010) makes the 2D coordinates support-independent.

line._note: exact 2D sketch coords in meters (from analyze_model(sketch))

arc.dir: 1 (CCW) | -1 (CW) — sweep sense, REQUIRED (centre+start+end alone describe two arcs); mirrors analyze_model(sketch)'s 'dir' and add_sketch_entity(arc_center)'s 'direction'

ellipse.x1: number (X of a point on the MAJOR axis)
ellipse.x2: number (X of a point on the MINOR axis)
ellipse._note: COVERED since v0.7.0. Exactly the shape analyze_model(sketch) reports and add_sketch_entity(ellipse) consumes — round-trips verbatim.

spline.points: array of FLAT through-point coordinates [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...] — >= 2 points (4 numbers), even count
spline._note: COVERED since v0.7.0. Mirrors analyze_model(sketch)'s spline 'points' (flat x,y list). HONEST CAVEAT (KNOWN-LIMITATIONS): recreating a spline from through-points is VISUALLY equivalent, not bit-identical (SW stores control points + tangency, not interpolation points) — volume/area round-trips within tolerance, never byte-exact.

profile_primitives._common_flag: any primitive may carry construction: true — created as CONSTRUCTION/reference geometry (mirrors analyze_model's per-segment flag)

extrude.description: Solid extrusion of a referenced sketch node. v0.5 adds explicit end conditions; 0.7.2 DOCUMENTS the long-implemented `reversed` flag.
extrude.sketch: string — id of a sketch node (must be the immediately preceding node — the extrude consumes the ACTIVE sketch)
extrude.end: string (optional) — 'blind' (default; requires depth) | 'through_all' | 'up_to_surface' (requires up_to) | 'mid_plane' (requires depth = the TOTAL width; extrudes symmetrically about the sketch plane). Back-compat: depth:'through_all'/'through' or through:true still mean through_all.
extrude.depth: number — meters (blind: the one-sided depth; mid_plane: the TOTAL symmetric width)
extrude.reversed: boolean (optional, default false) — extrude toward the datum's NEGATIVE normal instead of the positive one (maps to the extrude tool's `reverse` param). Default direction is +normal: Front→+Z, Top→+Y, Right→+X. IGNORED by mid_plane (symmetric by construction). THE HIGH-RISK FLAG ON THE REVERSE PATH: a boss on 'front' grows toward the direction the front view is looked at FROM, so WITHOUT `reversed` the sketch plane is the part's BACK face and every subsequent depth is measured from the wrong end — which produces a MIRRORED part that volume, area and topology all report as correct (recipe R6/R14; observed for real on f-2, IR-ADR-019).
extrude.up_to: object (up_to_surface only) — { face: face_anchor } : the face the feature terminates on, as a geometric anchor (+ optional hint)
extrude.merge: boolean (optional, default true) - false: the boss stays a SEPARATE body (a multi-body part for tab_slot)

revolve.description: Solid of revolution of the referenced sketch node (COVERED since v0.5.1 — grown for the 1-2 flange). The profile sketch should contain the axis segment (typically the construction centerline of the half-section, the classic revolve idiom); the compiler passes the axis segment's 2D coordinates and the tool selects it in the active sketch and treats it as the centerline.
revolve.sketch: string — id of a sketch node (must be the immediately preceding node — the revolve consumes the ACTIVE sketch)
revolve.axis: { x1, y1, x2, y2 } — the axis SEGMENT's exact 2D sketch coordinates (meters), from analyze_model(sketch); normally the sketch's construction centerline
revolve.angle: number — RADIANS (default 6.283185 = 360°, matching the recipe's SI dimension; the compiler converts to the tool boundary's degrees, C4)

sweep.description: Swept solid (boss) along a path sketch (COVERED since v0.7.0 — forward-vocabulary session, IR-ADR-017). Lowers to extrude_feature(sweep). GRAMMAR: the PROFILE sketch node must IMMEDIATELY precede the sweep (the tool consumes the ACTIVE sketch as the profile, like extrude); the PATH is an EARLIER sketch node referenced by id — the compiler substitutes its RUNTIME sketch name (node_feature mechanism, localization/numbering-proof, same as loft's profiles). So the node order is: path sketch, ..., profile sketch, sweep. Boss-only (the execution surface has no sweep cut).
sweep.sketch: string — id of the PROFILE sketch node (must be the immediately preceding node)
sweep.path: string — id of an EARLIER sketch node holding the sweep path (an open line/arc chain; must not be the profile sketch)

rib.description: Rib feature from an OPEN profile sketch (COVERED since v0.5.2 — grown for the 2-1 angle bracket; required the NEW create_rib execution tool). The profile is typically a single line whose extensions hit existing walls (e.g. the diagonal between an L-bracket's legs); SolidWorks extends and thickens it.
rib.sketch: string — id of a sketch node (must be the immediately preceding node — the rib consumes the ACTIVE sketch)
rib.two_sided: boolean (optional, default true — thicken symmetrically about the sketch)
rib.reverse_thickness_dir: boolean (optional, default false — SINGLE-SIDED ribs only (two_sided=false): thicken the opposite side of the sketch normal; passthrough added v0.7.0)
rib.reverse_material_dir: boolean (optional, default false — which side the rib fills toward; a wrong value is auto-recovered by the tool's flipped retry)
rib.is_norm_to_sketch: boolean (optional, default false — false = extrusion parallel to the sketch, the classic line rib)

linear_pattern.description: Linear feature pattern along a canonical axis (COVERED since v0.7.0 — forward-vocabulary session, IR-ADR-017). Lowers to create_pattern(linear); the seed is an earlier feature-producing node whose RUNTIME feature name the compiler substitutes (node_feature, same as circular_pattern). SINGLE direction by design: the execution tool's documented count2/spacing2 second direction was never wired in C# (no D2 entity is selected — recorded tool-surface gap); a GRID composes as a pattern OF a pattern (linear_pattern seeding on an earlier linear_pattern node).
linear_pattern.feature: string — id of an earlier feature-producing node: the pattern seed
linear_pattern.direction: string — 'x' | 'y' | 'z' (canonical model axis; the tool selects the default plane whose normal is that axis)
linear_pattern.spacing: number — meters (> 0): distance between adjacent instances
linear_pattern.count: integer >= 2 — total instances incl. the seed
linear_pattern.flip: boolean (optional, default false — pattern toward the NEGATIVE axis; exposed v0.7.0 via FeatureLinearPattern3's FlipDir1)

circular_pattern.description: Circular feature pattern (COVERED since v0.5.1). References an EARLIER feature-producing node as the seed — the compiler substitutes that node's RUNTIME-created feature name (localization-proof, same principle as the offset-plane name) — and creates the pattern axis from two datum planes' intersection.
circular_pattern.feature: string — id of an earlier feature-producing node (see covered_subset.feature_producers for the registered list): the pattern seed
circular_pattern.axis: { datums: [d1, d2] } — two DISTINCT canonical datums ('front'|'top'|'right') whose intersection is the pattern axis (front∩right = the Y axis, etc.); the compiler creates the reference axis and threads its runtime name
circular_pattern.count: integer >= 2 — total instances incl. the seed
circular_pattern.angle_deg: number — DEGREES; with equal_spacing=true the TOTAL spread (360 = full ring), else the spacing BETWEEN instances (reproduce the recipe's CirPattern verbatim: count=instances, angle_deg=spacing_deg, equal_spacing as reported — see create_pattern's round-trip guidance)

hole.description: Parametric hole. Encapsulates sketch+cut; the compiler expands it (resolve top face -> create_sketch(on_face, face_index) -> circle at centre -> through cut).
hole.ref: node_face + position (e.g. top face of n1, center)
hole.fully_define: boolean (optional) — overrides the graph's fully_define_sketches for the hole's own sketch (a sketch_fully_define right before the through cut)
hole.depth: number — meters, or 'through_all' (v0.5 supports 'through_all' only; 'through' accepted as an alias)

fillet.description: 3D edge fillet (post-solid, NOT a sketch fillet). Lowers to add_edge_feature(fillet, edge_indices) after the resolver matches each edge anchor against live analyze_model(edges) midpoints. THE reference-model testbed — every lesson here feeds P1.3. v0.8.0: an edge anchor may carry its OWN `radius` - then ONE multiple-radius fillet feature is made (the 12 outline corners of an unfolded blank); `radius` is the default for the anchors without one.
fillet.radius: number - meters (> 0); optional when EVERY edge anchor carries a radius of its own
fillet.edges: array of edge_anchor objects (>= 1): [{ near: [x,y,z], hint?: string, radius?: number }] - one per filleted edge, midpoints from the ORIGINAL part's analyze_model(edges)

chamfer.description: 3D edge chamfer (post-solid; COVERED since v0.5.3 — grown for level-2-2). Same HYBRID edge-anchor reference model as fillet (IR-ADR-008): each anchor's `near` is the target edge's midpoint from the PRE-chamfer geometry (the chamfer consumes those edges), matched against live analyze_model(edges) on the rebuild. Lowers to add_edge_feature(chamfer, edge_indices).
chamfer.distance: number — meters (> 0): the first-face setback (D1), always required
chamfer.angle: number — RADIANS (distance_angle only; default 0.785398 = 45°; the compiler converts to the tool boundary's degrees, C4)
chamfer.distance2: number — meters (> 0; distance_distance only, required there): the second-face setback (D2)
chamfer.flip: boolean (optional, default false; distance_distance is directional — flip swaps which face gets D1 vs D2, auto-recoverable like rib's reverse)
chamfer.edges: array of edge_anchor objects (>= 1): [{ near: [x,y,z], hint?: string }] — one per chamfered edge, midpoints from the PRE-chamfer state's analyze_model(edges)

loft.description: Multi-profile boss loft / blend (COVERED since v0.5.4 — grown for level-2-2's Loft2 frustum). Lowers to extrude_feature(loft, profiles=[...]). UNLIKE extrude/revolve/rib, the loft selects its profile sketches BY NAME (not the active sketch), so the profile sketch nodes need NOT immediately precede the loft — they are ordinary earlier sketch nodes (each on its own plane/offset) that the loft references by id. The compiler threads each referenced sketch's RUNTIME name (recorded from create_sketch's activeSketch — localization/numbering-proof, same principle as circular_pattern's seed). v0.5.4 = a simple boss blend (no guide curves / start-end tangency); those are future growth.
loft.profiles: array of >= 2 sketch node ids, IN LOFT ORDER — the profiles the loft blends through (e.g. ["n10","n11"] for a two-circle frustum). Each must reference an EARLIER sketch node.

sheet_metal.description: Sheet-metal BASE FLANGE (COVERED since v0.5.5 — grown for 4-1). Converts the referenced sketch profile into the sheet blank and establishes the sheet definition (thickness / default bend radius / K-factor). Lowers to sheet_metal_feature(base_flange). The tree's SheetMetal definition feature and Flat-Pattern are byproducts — they are NOT separate IR nodes. v0.8.0: an optional SHEET-METAL GAUGE TABLE (gauge_table + gauge): the thickness, radius and K-factor come from the table row.
sheet_metal.sketch: string — id of a sketch node (must be the immediately preceding node — the base flange consumes the ACTIVE sketch)
sheet_metal.thickness: number - meters (> 0); optional when gauge_table is given (the table row decides)
sheet_metal.bend_radius: number (optional — default bend radius in meters; omitted = thickness)
sheet_metal.reverse_thickness: boolean (optional, default false — thicken to the OPPOSITE side of the sketch plane. A wrong side puts every downstream bend-sketch plane off the sheet. PREFER reproducing the original's own flag (analyze_model(features) reports it on the SMBaseFlange) over deriving from face positions — see symmetric_thickness for why)
sheet_metal.symmetric_thickness: boolean (optional, default false — thicken BOTH ways off the sketch plane, ±t/2 mid-plane style. Reproduce the ORIGINAL's own flag (analyze_model(features) reports it on the SMBaseFlange): the thickness-direction flags also define the intrinsic sheet orientation that downstream bend directions fold against — an identical blank B-rep built via reverse flags folded 4-1's Bend1 the MIRRORED way)
sheet_metal.gauge_table: string (optional) - the FULL path of a SolidWorks sheet-metal gauge table (.xlsx); with `gauge`
sheet_metal.gauge: string - the gauge exactly as the table spells it (e.g. '16 Gauge'); required with gauge_table (a wrong one lists the table's)
sheet_metal.gauge_radius: number (optional) - meters: one of the table row's radii (default the first)

sketched_bend.description: Sketched bend (SM3dBend; COVERED since v0.5.5 — grown for 4-1's five bends). Bends the sheet about the bend LINE(S) in the referenced sketch — a sketch with N bend lines yields ONE feature with N bends (4-1's Sketch6). Lowers to sheet_metal_feature(sketched_bend). The FIXED side is a 3D pick point: SolidWorks derives which half stays put from the POINT, so this anchor carries side semantics, not just face identity.
sketched_bend.sketch: string — id of a sketch node holding the bend line(s) (must be the immediately preceding node — the bend consumes the ACTIVE sketch)
sketched_bend.angle: number — RADIANS (default 1.570796 = 90°, the recipe's SI dimension; the compiler converts to the tool boundary's degrees, C4)
sketched_bend.radius: number (optional — bend radius in meters; OMITTED = the sheet's default radius, matching a recipe sketched_bend block with no radius)
sketched_bend.flip: boolean (optional, default false — reverse the bend direction; replay the recipe's `flip`)
sketched_bend.fixed: { near: [x,y,z], hint?: string } — a 3D point (meters) ON the sheet face, on the SIDE that must stay put, in the PRE-bend geometry (the state the rebuild is in when the bend executes). Passed straight through as the tool's fixed_x/y/z coordinate pick (no index resolution — the point IS the side selector).

mirror.description: Feature mirror about a canonical datum plane (MirrorPattern; COVERED since v0.5.5 — grown for 4-1's Mirror1, which mirrors its two edge flanges about Right Plane). Lowers to create_pattern(mirror) with the referenced nodes' RUNTIME feature names (node_feature mechanism, localization-proof). NOTE (live-verified): SolidWorks refuses to mirror a bare SM3dBend sketched bend — mirror flanges/cuts/bosses; 4-1 mirrors edge flanges.
mirror.plane: { datum: 'front' | 'top' | 'right' } — the mirror plane (canonical; the compiler passes the canonical English name, resolved language-independently)
mirror.features: array of >= 1 earlier feature-producing node ids — the features to mirror, in tree order

edge_flange.description: Edge flange (EdgeFlange; COVERED since v0.5.6 — 4-1's last vocabulary gap). TWO MODES since v0.7.0: (A) CUSTOM PROFILE (the reverse-replay mode) — frame + profile given. SELF-CONTAINED node: no preceding sketch node — the flange API only accepts a profile sketch IT generated (InsertSketchForEdgeFlange), so the compiler generates it, CLEARS the default rectangle, redraws `profile`, then creates the flange (sheet_metal_feature edge_flange_sketch → add_sketch_entity* → edge_flange_finish). The generated sketch's frame is UNPREDICTABLE, hence `frame` is REQUIRED there (IR-ADR-010 transform). (B) SIMPLE LENGTH (the forward mode, v0.7.0/IR-ADR-017) — `length` given INSTEAD of frame+profile: a full-edge-width flange of that length, lowered to ONE sheet_metal_feature(edge_flange) call with the anchor-resolved edge_index. Length mode accepts only edge + angle + length (position stays the tool default material_inside, radius = the sheet default, flip unsupported — use mode A when you need those). The length is the OUTER dimension: measured to the outer virtual sharp (the tool's dimension_type default since 2026-10-28; SolidWorks otherwise reuses the last choice made in its own interface), so a plate of thickness t with a flange of length L stands L tall overall.
edge_flange.edge: { near: [x,y,z], hint?: string } — a 3D point (meters) ON the attach edge, in the geometry state when this node executes (the reader's edge_flange.edges[].mid — ground-truth readback, IR-ADR-014). Mutually exclusive with `edges`.
edge_flange.edges: array of anchors { near: [x,y,z], hint? } (>= 2; MODE B only, needs `length`, mutually exclusive with `edge`) — ONE multi-edge flange: EVERY edge that shares the parameters is one feature (user rule, Phase 7 post-mortem: 'edgeflange5,6,7,8 should have been one feature'). Lowers to ONE sheet_metal_feature(edge_flange, edge_indices). Neighbouring flanges meet in a tight corner with a 0.003 in gap (`gap`); never one node per edge.
edge_flange.gap: number — meters (> 0; MODE B with `edges`, optional; default 0.0000762 = 0.003 in): the gap between neighbouring flanges at a corner (tight, weld-ready)
edge_flange.limits: array of { edge?: integer (index into `edges`, default 0), from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z] } — MODE B only, needs `length`: PARTIAL FLANGES inside the same feature. The generated profile of that edge is shortened to the stretch from..to along it (METERS; the stretch that KEEPS its flange; a profile only shrinks). A lip that stops 5/16 in short of a corner, a return flange stopped 0.313 in from the bottom and 0.312 in below the top bend. Lowers to sheet_metal_feature(profile_limits); the flange is checked by its own error code and the old extent restored when it fails.
edge_flange.angle_exact: boolean (optional, default false) — HARD DEFAULT 90 DEGREES: an `angle` within 5 degrees of 90 is snapped to exactly 90 by the tool; set true ONLY when the user stated that angle (an angle read off a picture is never exact)
edge_flange.angle: number — RADIANS (default 1.570796 = 90°; the compiler converts to the tool boundary's degrees, C4). Within 5° of 90° it is snapped to exactly 90° unless `angle_exact`.
edge_flange.length: number — meters (> 0; MODE B only, mutually exclusive with frame/profile): the flange length along the bend direction
edge_flange.radius: number (optional, MODE A only — bend radius in meters; OMITTED = the sheet's default radius)
edge_flange.position: string (optional, MODE A only — 'material_inside' (tool default) | 'material_outside' | 'bend_outside' | 'centerline' | 'bend_sharp'; replay the recipe edge_flange block's `position` verbatim — 4-1's Edge-Flange1 is bend_outside)
edge_flange.flip: boolean (optional, MODE A only, default false — InsertSketchForEdgeFlange's FlipDir; at 90° the flange plane is flip-invariant and the frame transform absorbs the orientation, but replay it when read)
edge_flange.frame: { origin, xdir, ydir } — the ORIGINAL profile sketch's frame (REQUIRED in mode A, ABSENT in mode B)
edge_flange.profile: array of profile primitives — the ORIGINAL profile sketch's segments, original 2D coords (line/arc/circle + construction flags, same grammar as sketch.profile; REQUIRED in mode A, ABSENT in mode B)

hem.description: Hem on the free edge(s) of flange walls (Hem; lowers to sheet_metal_hem). ALL edges of one node make ONE feature. The hem folds toward the side of the edge you pick: the OUTER top edge of a wall folds outward, the INNER one inward. 'double' hems are refused by SolidWorks and not offered.
hem.edges: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1) - a point ON the free edge on top of a flange wall
hem.hem_type: 'closed' (default; its gap is fixed at 0.1 mm) | 'open' (always 180 degrees) | 'tear_drop' (180 < angle < 270 degrees, default 225) | 'rolled' (angle < 360 degrees, default 180)
hem.length: number - meters (> 0): the hem length (SolidWorks' default when omitted)
hem.gap: number - meters (> 0): the gap of an open / tear-drop / rolled hem
hem.angle: number - RADIANS (> 0): tear_drop and rolled hems only
hem.radius: number - meters (> 0): the hem's bend radius (default the sheet's)
hem.miter_gap: number - meters (> 0): the gap at mitred corners
hem.k_factor: number in (0, 1): a K-factor for the hem's bends

break_corner.description: Break (round or chamfer) the corners of flange walls (Break-Corner; sheet_metal_break_corner). Many faces make ONE feature. It needs the planar face of a flange wall - an edge, a wall's end face or the base flange's face beside flanges is refused. A 45 degree chamfer is how a wall end is cut for a mitre.
break_corner.faces: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1) - a point ON a flange wall's planar face (outer or inner)
break_corner.distance: number - meters (> 0): the fillet radius / chamfer length

corner_relief.description: CORNER RELIEF (sheet_metal_corner_relief): the relief cut where the bends of two walls (two_bend) or three bends (three_bend) meet at a corner - ONE feature for EVERY corner of that type of the body (the open corners of a tray of edge flanges; the mitred corner where a flange runs round a bend). Five relief types were built and measured on two-bend corners; a three-bend corner takes the rectangular relief only; the other three-bend reliefs kill SolidWorks on two-bend corners and are not offered.
corner_relief.corner_type: 'two_bend' (default) | 'three_bend' (three bends meet; 'relief' must be 'rectangular' and `length` is required, e.g. the outer bend radius = inside radius + thickness)
corner_relief.body: string (optional): the NAME of the solid body to relieve - required when the part has several solid bodies
corner_relief.relief: 'circular' (default; `width` is the diameter, at least 2 x the thickness) | 'square' | 'rectangular' (`length` is the side; ONE cut - SolidWorks stores a square relief as a rectangular one) | 'tear' (fixed by the geometry) | 'obround' (a slot about twice as long as wide: `length` and `width`)
corner_relief.width: number - meters (> 0): the diameter of a circular relief / the width of an obround one (default 2 x the thickness)
corner_relief.length: number - meters (> 0): the side of a square / rectangular relief / the length of an obround one (required for those; default 2 x the thickness)
corner_relief.add_filleted_corners: boolean (optional; needs fillet_diameter; square / rectangular reliefs take it, circular ones ignore it)

closed_corner.description: Closed Corner (sheet_metal_corners): the wall END FACE at a corner is extended so it closes the corner gap. One face per corner; every corner gets its own Closed Corner feature, in order.
closed_corner.faces: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1) - a point ON the wall end face that points at its neighbour across the corner gap
closed_corner.gap: number - meters (>= 0): the corner gap (default 0.0762 mm = 0.003 in)

miter_flange.description: ONE mitre flange along a chain of edges (sheet_metal_miter_flange): a closed loop of four edges gives weld-tight mitred corners all round in a single feature (rim, lip). The profile is generated at the sheet edge at the START of the chain, on the sheet's end face. Give exactly ONE of height / profile_points / profile_sketch.
miter_flange.edges: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1), IN ORDER along the chain - a point ON each edge
miter_flange.height: number - meters (> 0): one straight wall `height` off the sheet face (with `angle`)
miter_flange.profile_points: array of [across, up] pairs (meters, >= 1): a POLYLINE from the chain start in the sheet's frame - up = off the sheet face, across = toward the sheet's interior (negative = outward); a wall + rim + lip is [[0,0.10],[0.019,0.10],[0.019,0.113]] = a bend at every vertex of every corner
miter_flange.profile_sketch: string - id of an EARLIER sketch node holding your own profile (on a plane through the start of the first edge)
miter_flange.dimension_profile: boolean (default true): the generated profile is fully defined, one dimension per segment (D1..Dn), so equations can drive it
miter_flange.angle: number - RADIANS, with `height` only: from the sheet's flat outward continuation; 90 degrees (default) = perpendicular
miter_flange.position: 'material_inside' (default; the flange's outer face is flush with the sheet's boundary) | 'material_outside' | 'bend_outside' | 'bend_centerline' | 'bend_sharp' | 'bend_tangent'
miter_flange.rip_gap: number - meters (>= 0): the gap at the mitres (default 0.0762 mm)

gusset.description: Sheet-metal GUSSET (SolidWorks' Rib) in the inside corner of a bend: the pressed 'rounded' rib or the 'flat' triangle (sheet_metal_gusset). `position` is where its centre stands along the bend, from the bend's start.
gusset.faces: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (EXACTLY 2) - a point ON each of the two faces the gusset joins: the sheet and the flange beside the bend
gusset.position: number - meters (> 0): where the gusset's CENTRE stands, measured along the bend from its START (the end with the lowest coordinate along it) - always where asked, however many gussets already stand on the bend (the tool measures SolidWorks' reference vertex and corrects)
gusset.indent_width: number - meters (> 0): the rib's inner faces are this far apart (both dimension schemes)
gusset.dimension_scheme: 'indent_depth' (default; needs indent_depth) | 'profile' (needs profile_length and profile_height or profile_angle)

jog.description: JOG: an offset step in a flat sheet - two parallel bends of opposite direction (sheet_metal_jog; built from two sketched bends at the closed-form distance, the far bend folded first). The sheet's face must lie in the Front plane (z = 0) and be flat; the flat blank does not change.
jog.line: [[x,y,z],[x,y,z]] - the FIRST bend line, a segment on the face (SolidWorks treats it as infinite)
jog.fixed: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the face on the side that stays put; the other side steps
jog.offset: number - meters (> 0): the plane-to-plane step h = the distance between the TOP faces of the two flat parts
jog.angle: number - RADIANS (> 0, at most 90 degrees; default 90 degrees): the angle of each bend
jog.direction: 'up' (default; the part beyond the jog steps toward +Z) | 'down'
jog.k_factor: number in (0, 1; default the part's global K)

tab_slot.description: TAB AND SLOT (sheet_metal_tab_slot): tabs on the edge of one body and matching slots in a face of another - a MULTI-BODY part (make the bodies with extrude merge=false). Tabs are spread equally between a start and an end offset along the edge; the node makes a Tab feature and a Slot feature.
tab_slot.edge: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the TAB EDGE: an edge of the tab body's face that lies ON the slot face (a wall's bottom edge)
tab_slot.slot_face: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the face of the OTHER body in which the slots are cut
tab_slot.tab_face: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (optional) - the tab body's face that TOUCHES the slot face (found by itself when omitted)
tab_slot.tab_length: number - meters (> 0): the length of each tab along the edge
tab_slot.start_offset: number - meters (>= 0): from the edge's START vertex
tab_slot.end_offset: number - meters (>= 0): from the edge's END vertex
tab_slot.slot_clearance: number - meters (> 0; default 0.1 mm): each slot is the tab plus this at both ends
tab_slot.tab_thickness: number - meters (> 0; default the thin side of the tab face)
tab_slot.tab_height: number - meters (> 0; default through the slot body)
tab_slot.edge_treatment_size: number - meters (> 0): required with a fillet / chamfer

move_face.description: MOVE FACE (move_face): move, offset or rotate faces of a body in ONE feature (e.g. the stepped corner tops of a closed-corner chassis).
move_face.faces: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1) - a point ON each face to move; several faces make one feature
move_face.distance: number - meters (> 0): every face moves this far along its normal (reverse = the other way)
move_face.translation: [dx, dy, dz] - meters: the displacement vector
move_face.rotation: {axis_point:[x,y,z], axis_direction:[x,y,z], angle: RADIANS} - the axis the faces turn about

forming_tool.description: FORMING TOOL of the design library (a .sldftp: louver, lance, emboss, extruded flange, rib) placed on a flat sheet face (sheet_metal_forming_tool). The tool forms the sheet AWAY from the face it is placed on (place it on the other face to form the other way); a bend or the edge of the sheet is refused, and a placement that would overhang the sheet's edge, use another configuration than the one asked or report a rebuild error is taken out again. A placed tool can seed a linear_pattern (a louver array).
forming_tool.tool: string - a bare name ('louver'), a path relative to the forming tools folder ('louvers/louver') or the full path of a .sldftp
forming_tool.at: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the flat sheet face = the PLACEMENT of the tool (the face is found by it)
forming_tool.rotation: number - RADIANS (default 0): counter-clockwise looking at the face from outside the part, about the placement point
forming_tool.configuration: string (optional) - a configuration of the tool file; one that does not exist is refused

lofted_bend.description: LOFTED BEND (sheet_metal_lofted_bend): a sheet-metal transition between two OPEN profile sketches on parallel planes (round-to-square duct, funnel). It creates the sheet-metal definition itself, so it must be the FIRST feature (only sketch nodes before it). Each profile is ONE continuous open chain of lines / arcs, the two of the same kind (an arc and an arc, a U and a U).
lofted_bend.profiles: array of EXACTLY 2 sketch node ids, in loft order - each an EARLIER sketch node
lofted_bend.thickness_side: 'side1' (default; material outside the first profile's curve) | 'side2' (inside)
lofted_bend.formed: boolean (default false: the faceted lofted bend; true: the smooth formed surface)
lofted_bend.facets: 'chord_tolerance' (default) | 'number_of_bends' | 'segment_length' | 'segment_angle': the ONE facet argument SolidWorks uses

swept_flange.description: SWEPT FLANGE (sheet_metal_swept_flange): sheet metal made by sweeping an open profile along a path (bracket, channel, flared rim). It creates the sheet-metal definition itself, so it must be the FIRST feature (only sketch nodes before it). The profile is an OPEN chain at the START of the path on a plane perpendicular to it (an L, a U, a Z, a single line); the path is a line, a path with a corner (mitred) or an arc.
swept_flange.profile: string - id of an EARLIER sketch node: the open profile
swept_flange.path: string - id of an EARLIER sketch node (not the profile's): the path
swept_flange.bend_radius: number - meters (> 0; default the thickness): the INSIDE radius
swept_flange.reverse: boolean (default false: the profile line is the OUTER face of the bends; true: the inner face)

from_flat.description: FOLD FROM FLAT (sheet_metal_from_flat): build the whole part from the flat pattern in an ASCII DXF (outline + straight bend lines), in the empty part - so it must be the FIRST node. Strategy 'sketched_bends' folds along the bend lines (a flat with closed corners is refused with BEND_NOT_FOLDABLE); 'miter_flange' rebuilds a one-profile mitre box (nested bend rings) with the flange recipe; 'auto' picks. The part's own flat pattern is checked against the DXF.
from_flat.dxf_path: string - the full path of the ASCII DXF
from_flat.angle: number - RADIANS (> 0; default 90 degrees): the angle of every bend
from_flat.directions: list of 'up' | 'down' (one per bend DEPTH, innermost first) or {'<depth>': 'up'|'down'}: the direction of each bend when the DXF does not say
from_flat.hidden_direction: 'up' (default) | 'down': what the HIDDEN bend linetype means
from_flat.fixed_point: [x, y] - meters in DXF coordinates: a point of the region that stays put
from_flat.reach_tolerance: number - meters (> 0): how far a region may reach across another bend line
from_flat.rip_gap: number - meters (>= 0): overrides the rip gap the recipe reads from the DXF

unfold.description: UNFOLD (flatten) the bends of the sheet-metal part (sheet_metal_fold): edit the flat blank in place (round its corners with one multi-radius fillet, trim with a surface cut), then `fold` it back with the SAME fixed face.
unfold.fixed_face: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the face that stays put (e.g. the back plate)

fold.description: FOLD the bends of the part back (sheet_metal_fold) after an `unfold` - use the SAME fixed face you unfolded with.
fold.fixed_face: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the face that stays put

flat_pattern.description: Flat-pattern options of the sheet-metal part (flat_pattern_control): corner treatment, merged faces ...; the Flat-Pattern is unsuppressed, the options applied and measured, and it is suppressed again unless leave_flat. Writing the flat DXF needs a SAVED part: use the flat_pattern_control tool after save_document.
flat_pattern.merge_faces: boolean (optional): false splits the flat faces
flat_pattern.leave_flat: boolean (default false): keep the part flat

sheet_metal_settings.description: Sheet-metal PARAMETERS of the part (sheet_metal_params set): the global K-factor, the bend-allowance model, the automatic relief, thickness / radius overrides. A document setting, not a tree feature.
sheet_metal_settings.thickness: number - meters (> 0): the base flange's override
sheet_metal_settings.bend_radius: number - meters (> 0): the base flange's override
sheet_metal_settings.reset_overrides: list of 'bend_allowance' | 'auto_relief' | 'bend_parameters': back to the document defaults

delete_face.description: DELETE FACE(S) of a solid so it becomes an open SURFACE body (delete_face) - the first step of the base shape of a rim-and-lip enclosure that is then offset and converted.
delete_face.faces: array of anchors {near:[x,y,z], hint?} (>= 1) - a point ON each face to delete

offset_surface.description: OFFSET SURFACE of one surface body (offset_surface): the recipe for a converted enclosure offsets the outer skin INWARD by one sheet thickness before convert_to_sheet_metal (reverse_thickness on), so the folded part keeps its outer size.
offset_surface.body: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the surface body
offset_surface.hide_original: boolean (default true): hide the original so the next picks hit the offset one

surface_extrude.description: SURFACE EXTRUDE of a sketch (surface_extrude): the profile becomes a SURFACE body - a ribbon for an open profile - used with surface_cut to trim an unfolded blank.
surface_extrude.sketch: string - id of an EARLIER sketch node
surface_extrude.mid_plane: boolean (default false): symmetric about the sketch plane, depth = the TOTAL width

surface_cut.description: SURFACE CUT (surface_cut): cut the solid with a surface made by an earlier surface_extrude. Unlike a solid cut it can be MIRRORED (mirror.features). The tool measures the volume it removed and takes the cut out again when it removed nothing or too much.
surface_cut.surface: string - id of an EARLIER surface_extrude node
surface_cut.flip: boolean (default false): false removes the side the surface normal points to
surface_cut.max_removed_volume: number - cubic meters (> 0): the safety net against a wrong flip

convert_to_sheet_metal.description: CONVERT TO SHEET METAL of a surface (or solid) body (sheet_metal_convert; the API cannot create this feature, so it is driven through the PropertyManager from inside SolidWorks - SolidWorks must be on screen). Pick ORDER matters: the fixed face first, then the lists in the order of `steps`. The recipe for a rim-and-lip enclosure: (1) the bend edges nearest the fixed face (the back plate's perimeter), (2) the rip sketches, (3) the next bend series (rim outer edges), (4) the third series (lip root edges).
convert_to_sheet_metal.fixed_face: {near:[x,y,z], hint?} - a point ON the face that stays put
convert_to_sheet_metal.steps: ordered array: {list:'bend', edges:[edge anchors]} (one anchor per bend edge, in pick order) | {list:'rip', sketches:[ids of EARLIER sketch nodes]} (one line each, ending at the body's vertices)
convert_to_sheet_metal.reverse_thickness: 'default' (= 'on': the material goes OUTSIDE the surface) | 'on' | 'off' (the surface is the outer skin)

validation_split.plan_time_planner: Structural + schema only: type is registered, required params present, node references (sketch/node ids) structurally resolvable, units correct, anchors well-formed ([x,y,z] numbers), arc dir in {1,-1}.
validation_split.compile_exec_time: Geometric validity: referenced face/edge actually exists after prior features, anchors resolve to exactly one entity (tolerance ball), hole fits within the face. Owned by compiler + reference resolver + execution — NOT the Planner.

example._intent: Create a 20mm hole at the center of the top face of a 100x100x20mm block.

example_v05_new_vocabulary._intent: Fragment showing every v0.5 addition at once: a path-profile sketch (line+arc+construction) on an OFFSET plane, a cut terminating up-to-surface, and an anchored edge fillet.

face.hint: top face of the 3mm base plate

assembly_types_v06._note: ASSEMBLY sub-vocabulary (v0.6.0 — Phase B, ADR-047). An assembly graph contains ONLY these types: components first (tree order), then mates (creation order). Components reference part FILES by path+hash (the V1 cache discipline extends) — part IRs are NEVER embedded. Out of scope first round (each hit = VOCABULARY_GAP, C5): in-context features, flexible subassemblies, component patterns, configurations beyond the referenced one.

component.description: One component OCCURRENCE (instance). Lowers to insert_component (AddComponent5) with the FULL transform; `fixed` is always sent explicitly (deterministic state).
component.source: { path: '<part file>', hash?: 'sha256:...' } — the part FILE this occurrence references; hash makes staleness loud (ADR-040)
component.fixed: boolean (optional, default false) — fixed occurrences take `transform` as their authoritative PLACEMENT; floating ones use it as the initial placement + verification ground truth (mates do the constraining)
component.transform: REQUIRED — 13 numbers: 3x3 rotation row-major + translation xyz (meters) + scale — exactly analyze_assembly(components)' reported layout

mate.description: One mate between two component occurrences. Lowers to add_mate (AddMate5) with INDEX-first entity selection: each side's COMPONENT-LOCAL anchor resolves to a face/edge index via analyze_assembly(faces|edges, component) (KNOWN-LIMITATIONS #6). Read the original's type/alignment/value from the ENUMS verbatim (C7) — display names are localized and unreliable; never derive them from resulting positions.
mate.alignment: 'aligned' | 'anti_aligned' | 'closest' (optional; record the reader's RESOLVED alignment verbatim)
mate.value: number (SI: meters for distance, RADIANS for angle — C4; the compiler converts to the tool boundary) — required for distance/angle
mate.sides: EXACTLY 2 × { component: <earlier component node id>, anchor: { kind: 'plane'|'cylinder'|'cone'|'sphere'|'line'|'circle' (the reader's swMateEntity2ReferenceType_e name, verbatim), near: [x,y,z] COMPONENT-LOCAL meters (map the original mate's assembly-space EntityParams through the inverse component transform — local anchors are transform-invariant), hint?: string } }
